objects.text: Christianity in Persia
A life on a true timescale · every card traces to the evidence ledger
Pentecost: Acts 2:9 names Parthians and Medes (a later tradition links them to Persia)
Kartir's inscriptions list Christians among the groups he struck down
Persecution under Shapur II; Simeon bar Sabbae executed
Synod at Seleucia-Ctesiphon: a catholicos for the Persian church
Synod of Markabta ends appeals to Roman bishops
Olopun reaches Chang'an, according to the Xi'an Stele
The Xi'an Stele is erected
Edict of Wuzong against foreign religions in China
Mongols take Baghdad; Doquz Khatun is said to protect Christians
Rabban Bar Sauma travels from the Mongol court to Rome and Paris
New Julfa founded at Isfahan (dating disputed)
Henry Martyn completes a Persian New Testament
Mission press at Urmia prints in the Syriac of the plain
War on the Urmia plain; Assyrians flee toward Hamadan
After the revolution: seats reserved for Armenians, Assyrians and Chaldeans
Latest census count of Christians; estimates remain contested
